zones.what: Deck 6 balcony cabins sit directly over the lifeboat/tender line, and forward Deck 6 cabins additionally face a large blue metal housing right in front of the balcony.
zones.effect: Looking straight down from the balcony you see boat tops or the metal housing instead of water; the horizon view outward is still open.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to anyone who wants to watch the water below the rail (e.g. spotting marine life, port approach); doesn't matter if you mainly care about the horizon/sunset view.
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com Deck 6 page: "All balcony cabins on this deck will either look down on deck 5 below or lifeboats," and "Forward cabins will have a large blue metal roof in front of the balcony that obstructs the view looking down" — identical wording verified present on Apex, Ascent and Beyond deck-6 pages (same class layout, not cross-class boilerplate).

zones.what: Deck 3 is the lowest cabin deck, sitting directly beneath Decks 4-5's casino, theatre, shops, Grand Plaza restaurants and Martini Bar.
zones.effect: Foot traffic, music and late-night activity from the venues above are audible in these cabins, more so than higher decks.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers should avoid Deck 3; bargain-hunters indifferent to noise can save money here.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com Editor's Review: "cruisers may want to steer clear of those on the third deck, as these are under the casino, restaurants, and some shops"; corroborated by cruisemummy.co.uk: "Just one deck up you'll find the theatre, The Club, shops, the casino, and several speciality restaurants."

zones.what: Eden is a three-deck venue built into the aft of Decks 4, 5 and 6, so Deck 7 aft cabins sit directly above its roof.
zones.effect: Eden runs live music and evening shows; guests directly above have reported the sound carrying into aft staterooms at night.
zones.mattersTo: Nightlife lovers may enjoy being close; light sleepers wanting quiet evenings should pick forward or midship instead.
zones.source: cruisemapper.com deck-6 plan: "Eden is a 3-deck high (aft-location on decks 4, 5, 6) lounge-bar-restaurant venue with live music" (confirmed identical placement on Edge, Apex, Beyond deck plans); cruisebooking.com Apex guide notes "aft staterooms on Deck 7 (directly above the Eden venue's nightly live shows)" for the same Eden layout.

zones.what: Deck 12 is the top cabin deck and sits directly beneath the Resort/Pool Deck (Deck 14) since Deck 13 is skipped in the numbering.
zones.effect: Early lounger-dragging, deck cleaning and pool-deck foot traffic can be heard from below, especially on sea days.
zones.mattersTo: Sea-day sleepers/late risers should avoid; pool-deck-adjacent convenience seekers may not mind.
zones.source: cruisegalore.com: "Midship cabins on Deck 12 (directly under the pool deck) can also get particularly noisy on sea days"; deck-skip pattern (12→14, no 13) confirmed on cruisedeckplans.com Edge deck list.

zones.what: Guests booking Prime Edge Stateroom (E1) on Deck 8 describe their location as sitting "on the hump" of the hull.
zones.effect: A first-person cruiser account distinguishes this location from the plain lifeboat-obstructed Deck 6 E3 cabins, implying a different (less boxed-in) balcony feel at the hull's outward step.
zones.mattersTo: Cabin-feel-sensitive travelers curious about hull-shape differences between decks; not something the cruise line itself labels as a distinct category.
zones.source: boards.cruisecritic.com forum post: "I've only sailed Edge once and we were on the hump on Deck 8 in an E1 cabin" (first-person account; no aggregator confirmation of a size/view benefit).

zones.what: On Edge-class ships the elevator banks sit midship, with staterooms stretching between them and the restaurants at either end of most decks.
zones.effect: Midship cabins get short walks to elevators (and reported hallway convenience without excess noise), while cabins toward the ends have a longer walk to dining venues.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited or elevator-dependent guests should favor midship; those wanting distance from elevator-bank foot traffic can go forward/aft instead.
zones.source: cruisemummy.co.uk: "on the Edge-class ships, the nearest elevators are mid-ship, and there are staterooms between them and the restaurants"; corroborated by a first-person Celebrity Edge YouTube walkthrough of elevator-to-stateroom proximity.

zones.what: Decks 11 and 12 are the highest and most forward/aft-reaching cabin decks on Celebrity Edge.
zones.effect: Pitching (bow) and swaying (stern) motion is most noticeable at the extreme ends of these top decks in rough seas.
zones.mattersTo: Motion-sensitive cruisers should avoid far forward/aft on Decks 11-12; those wanting the biggest view and top-deck proximity may accept the trade-off.
zones.source: cruisemummy.co.uk: "On Celebrity Edge, that means you may want to avoid cabins situated at the very front or rear of Decks 11 and 12... Combine that with the extra elevation on the upper decks, and you'll feel the movement far more."

zones.what: Infinite Veranda cabins use a single powered blackout shade covering the whole glass wall rather than separate curtains for bed and sitting areas.
zones.effect: Raising or lowering the shade lightens or darkens the entire room at once, which is a problem if one person wants to sleep while another wants light or an early view.
zones.mattersTo: Roommates/couples with different wake times or light sensitivity should be aware; solo travelers or same-schedule couples are unaffected.
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com: "there is only a power shade on the verandah and will darken the whole room when closed and brighten the whole room when open. This is a concern if your room mate still wants to sleep" (identical note verified across Edge, Apex and Beyond category pages, confirming it's a class-wide design trait).

zones.what: The Magic Carpet is a cantilevered platform on the starboard side that stops at various decks (including guest-cabin decks) and hosts bars/gatherings.
zones.effect: When the platform is docked near a cabin's deck, crowd noise and mechanical movement can reach nearby staterooms and reduce balcony privacy.
zones.mattersTo: Guests wanting a quiet balcony should check if their cabin is near a Magic Carpet stop; people who enjoy activity/energy may like it.
zones.source: cruisebooking.com Celebrity Edge guide: "The Magic Carpet's movement can lead to the gathering of people, which in turn can lead to noise... your moment of relaxing on the balcony may not be as tranquil as you wanted."

zones.what: Celebrity Edge offers 178 connecting staterooms across its Edge/Porthole/Single categories.
zones.effect: Families or groups can link adjoining rooms via an interior connecting door, unusual in this concentration versus older Celebrity classes.
zones.mattersTo: Families/groups traveling together benefit; solo/couple travelers may hear more through a connecting door than a standard wall.
zones.source: celebritycruises.com veranda staterooms page: "170 possible options of connecting staterooms make it easier than ever for families and friends to connect at sea"; cruisemapper.com cabin page confirms 178 connecting cabins fleet-wide on Edge.

zones.what: Wheelchair-accessible cabins are concentrated in specific room-number clusters: E1 accessible cabins 8230-8236 and 8239-8245 on Deck 8, plus scattered accessible Oceanview/Sky Suite rooms (8106, 8109, 9108, 9113, 9210, 10182, 10180 area).
zones.effect: Accessible-cabin seekers have the widest choice on Deck 8; other decks have only one or two accessible rooms per category.
zones.mattersTo: Wheelchair users planning ahead should target Deck 8 for the most accessible-cabin options.
zones.source: cruisemapper.com Celebrity Edge cabins page listing handicap cabin numbers by deck; cruiseline.com category E1 page: "Wheelchair Accessible Staterooms: 8230-8236 and 8239-8245."

leads.claim: Listed as having partially obstructed veranda views on Celebrity's own deck-plan PDF and on cruisedeckplans.com.
leads.source: celebritycorporatekit.com official 2019-20 Edge deck-plans PDF; cruisedeckplans.com Deck 6 page

leads.claim: Obstructed-view Prime Edge Infinite Veranda staterooms per Celebrity's own category notes.
leads.source: cruiseline.com category E1 page (sourced from Celebrity stateroom notes)

leads.claim: Obstructed-view Edge Infinite Veranda staterooms per Celebrity's own category notes.

Full official list of partially-obstructed-veranda staterooms spanning Decks 6-11, beyond just the lifeboat line — likely a mix of lifeboat, Magic Carpet-track, and structural-overhang obstructions that were not individually differentiated in the source.
leads.source: celebritycorporatekit.com official 2019-20 Celebrity Edge Deck Plans PDF

leads.claim: First-person reviewer reported the balcony view was ~40% blocked by the hull jutting out, poor soundproofing letting in Grand Plaza music/vibration, and cigarette smoke drifting in.
Reviewer noted the glazing bar sits at eye-level when seated, so standing gives a better view; otherwise no obstruction complaint.

unknowns: No ship-specific evidence found for i95 crew corridor access points or where they create service traffic near guest cabins on Edge.
No ship-specific evidence found tying bow-thruster noise (far forward, low decks) or anchor-chain noise to particular Edge cabins.
Engine/Azipod propulsion vibration by specific deck/section not documented for Edge itself with adequate confidence (only generic, unverified claims found for a sister ship).
No evidence found of a hull-taper effect (inward hull step hiding the straight-down view) on Edge's highest decks (15/16, Edge Villas/Iconic Suite/Rooftop Garden area).
Whether lifeboat obstruction meaningfully extends to Deck 7 (one deck above the confirmed Deck 6 lifeboat line) is unconfirmed — only Deck 6 has direct sourcing.
Exact deck/section for cabins reported as noisy from Sunset Bar specifically (as opposed to Eden or Rooftop Garden) could not be pinned down.
Whether Deck 8's reported 'hump' comes with a measurable size or obstruction difference versus neighboring decks is unconfirmed beyond one forum anecdote.
